definition: Spare EC2 capacity at up to 90 percent off On-Demand. AWS can reclaim it with a two-minute warning. Remember: use it only for fault-tolerant, interruptible work like batch jobs.

term: Compute vs EC2 Instance Savings Plans
definition: Compute Savings Plans work across any family, Region, Fargate, and Lambda, up to 66 percent off. EC2 Instance Savings Plans lock one family in one Region, up to 72 percent.
Reserves EC2 capacity in one Availability Zone for any length of time, with no term commitment. You pay On-Demand rates whether used or not. Remember: guarantees capacity, not a discount.
Packs instances close together in one Availability Zone for the lowest latency and highest throughput between them. Remember: ideal for HPC, but one hardware or zone failure hits everything.
Spread: each instance on distinct hardware, max seven running per Availability Zone, for small critical sets. Partition: up to seven rack-separated partitions per zone, for Hadoop, Cassandra, Kafka.
A virtual network card with its own private IP, MAC address, and security groups, bound to one Availability Zone. Remember: move a secondary ENI to a standby instance for failover.
Saves RAM to an encrypted EBS root volume, so the instance resumes with memory intact. Must be enabled at launch. Remember: instance store roots cannot hibernate.

term: EBS volume types at a glance
definition: gp3 and gp2 are general purpose SSD. io1 and io2 give sustained high IOPS. st1 suits throughput-heavy big data. sc1 is cheapest for cold data. Only SSD types can boot.
gp3 sets IOPS and throughput independently of size, now up to 80,000 IOPS. io2 Block Express reaches 256,000 IOPS with sub-millisecond latency and 99.999 percent durability.
Attach one io1 or io2 volume to up to 16 Nitro instances in the same Availability Zone. Needs a cluster-aware file system. Remember: not gp3, and never across zones.
Physical disks on the EC2 host with very high IOPS. Data survives a reboot but is lost on stop, hibernate, or termination. Remember: buffers, caches, and scratch data only.
Moves rarely needed snapshots to a tier about 75 percent cheaper. Restoring takes 24 to 72 hours, with a 90-day minimum. Remember: long-term compliance retention.
Retention rules keep deleted EBS snapshots and AMIs recoverable for 1 day to 1 year. Remember: the answer for protection against accidental deletion.
You cannot encrypt a volume in place. Snapshot it, copy or restore with encryption using a KMS key, then attach the new volume. Encryption by default only covers new volumes.
EBS is block storage for one instance in one Availability Zone. EFS is a shared NFS file system for many Linux instances across zones. Remember: EFS does not support Windows.
Standard for active files, Infrequent Access for files read a few times a quarter, Archive for a few times a year. Lifecycle management moves files between them automatically.
ALB is layer 7 HTTP with path and host routing. NLB is layer 4 TCP and UDP with static IPs per zone. GWLB is layer 3, for third-party appliances.
Spreads traffic evenly across all registered targets in every zone. ALB: on by default, no inter-zone charge. NLB and GWLB: off by default, inter-zone data is billed.
Sends a client to the same target each time, using a cookie on ALB or source IP on NLB. Remember: helps with local session state but can unbalance load.
Server Name Indication lets one listener serve many TLS certificates, chosen by hostname. Supported by ALB, NLB, and CloudFront. Remember: Classic Load Balancer allows only one certificate.
Also called connection draining. Lets in-flight requests finish before a deregistering target is removed. Default 300 seconds, range 0 to 3600. Set it low for short requests.
Target tracking holds a metric at a target value. Step and simple scaling react to CloudWatch alarms. Scheduled handles known times. Predictive forecasts recurring patterns from history.
After a simple scaling activity, the group waits, 300 seconds by default, before scaling again. Target tracking and step policies use instance warmup instead. A golden AMI shortens startup.
